STEP 1 - Scene: The meal is three small pieces of cheese pizza on a square white plate. It looks like cafeteria-style pizza with a thin-to-medium crust. The tortilla dish at the left edge belongs to another meal and is excluded.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square dinner plate, about 26 cm across.
- Taking 26 cm as the diameter, the area is 3.14 × 13² ≈ 530 cm².
- A square plate would have slightly more area, but the 530 cm² basis is used here.

STEP 3 - Items: Cheese pizza (crust, tomato sauce and mozzarella), in three pieces.

STEP 4 - Area:
| Piece | Size | Area |
|---|---|---|
| Top-left | ~10 × 9 cm | ~80 cm² |
| Top-right triangle | ~11 × 9 cm | ~65 cm² |
| Bottom | ~12 × 8 cm | ~85 cm² |

The pieces total about 230 cm², which is roughly 43% of the plate. Food covers about 43% of the plate, so this matches.

STEP 5 - Volume: 230 cm² × 1.2 cm average height ≈ 276 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: 276 ml × 0.6 g/ml ≈ 165 g.
- A bread-like slice would normally be 0.9–1.0 g/ml.
- Pizza has an airy crust, so I used about 0.6 g/ml as the effective bulk density.

STEP 7 - Energy: Cheese pizza is about 270 kcal per 100 g, so 165 g × 2.7 ≈ 445 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Three small pizza pieces at roughly 55 g each is plausible, and so is about 445 kcal.
